newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm, interest in Malaysian stock.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm, interest in Malaysian stock.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer on Monday in line with the gains on Wall Street, but dealers said focus was on Malaysian counters.
"There is nothing much going on apart from activity in the second board Malaysian counters," a dealer with a local institution said.
He said these stocks were "UMNO stocks", which typically become active at election times. UMNO, the United Malays National Organisation, is Malaysia's main political party.
Malaysian stock Metroplex Bhd and UIC Ltd led the actives with 3.2 million and 2.9 million shares.

Trading of Metroplex shares was suspended mid-morning pending an announcement with the stock unchanged at S$1.68. Some dealers speculated the announcement could be linked to its casino investment in the Philippines.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 14.11 points by mid-morning, at 2,142.60. Volume was at 42.8 million shares with gainers leading losers at 189 to 34.
Seaview Hotel led the gainers, up S$0.40 at S$14.00 on 12,000 shares. Dealers linked the gains to optimism surrounding its development of a car park.
